question: Under the Football Association's first laws of 1863, when was a player offside?
answer: Whenever he was ahead of the ball. As in rugby, a player in front of the ball could not take part in play, so passing forward to a team-mate was impossible and teams advanced by dribbling in packs. In 1866 the rule was relaxed: three opponents between attacker and goal made him onside.
move: Look at what a rule forbids to see which game its makers had in mind.
source: Harvey, Football: The First Hundred Years, 2005
reference: Harvey, Football: The First Hundred Years: The Untold Story, Routledge, 2005
